q: Which describes 'fairness' as a responsible AI dimension?
o: Considering the impact of the system on different groups of people and avoiding unjust differences
Making the model cost the same for everyone
Giving every model the same name
e: Fairness means measuring and reducing disparate outcomes across groups.

q: Which SageMaker capability continuously monitors deployed models for bias drift over time?
o: SageMaker Model Monitor working with SageMaker Clarify
e: Model Monitor can schedule bias drift and feature-attribution drift checks using Clarify.

q: Why is it important to tell users they are interacting with an AI system?
o: It is part of transparency and helps users judge how much to rely on the answers
e: Disclosure builds appropriate trust and is increasingly required by regulation.

q: Which is an example of a safety control for a generative AI image app?
o: Content filters that block violent or explicit image generation
e: Safety controls such as content filters, prompt checks and output moderation prevent harmful generations. Rekognition content moderation can also screen images.

q: What is the main concern with using copyrighted material to fine-tune a model without permission?
o: Possible intellectual property infringement and legal liability
e: Training or generating from content you don't have rights to creates IP risk. Check licences and data provenance.

q: Which describes 'privacy and security' in responsible AI?
o: Protecting personal data and models from misuse and unauthorised access
e: Privacy and security cover how data is collected, used, protected and kept from leaking through outputs.

q: A company finds its chatbot sometimes reveals customers' phone numbers. Which control most directly helps?
o: Sensitive information filters (PII redaction) in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
e: Guardrails can detect and block or mask personal data in prompts and responses. Also keep PII out of retrievable data where possible.

q: Which describes 'governance' in responsible AI?
o: Policies, processes and oversight that ensure AI is developed and used responsibly
e: Governance includes accountability, approval processes, documentation, audits and monitoring.

q: What does human-centred design mean for an AI product?
o: Designing around users' real needs, with clear explanations and easy ways to correct or override AI
e: Human-centred design keeps people informed and in control and makes AI limits clear.
an: Cooking shows a code-computed diff of exactly what an AI recipe change would alter, with Accept and Deny, instead of quietly rewriting the recipe.

q: Which data characteristics help produce a fair and reliable model? (Choose TWO.)
e: Good datasets are inclusive, diverse, balanced, accurate and curated, with documented sources.

q: Which describes 'subgroup analysis' in bias evaluation?
o: Comparing model performance across different demographic groups
Splitting the model into smaller models
e: Checking metrics per group reveals whether some groups get worse outcomes.

q: Why is ongoing monitoring part of responsible AI, not just testing before launch?
o: Data and usage change over time, so new biases or failures can appear after deployment
Testing is not allowed before launch
e: Drift, new user behaviour and adversarial use mean risks must be watched continuously.
an: RPGACE's error log captures real failures automatically and flags the feature they belong to, instead of assuming 'it worked once, so it works'.

q: What is 'toxicity' when evaluating generative AI output?
o: Rude, hateful or harmful content in the model's output
e: Toxicity is one of the safety measures checked in evaluations and filtered by guardrails.

q: Which is an environmental consideration when choosing AI solutions responsibly?
o: Larger models and more training use more energy, so choose the right-sized model
Energy use is unrelated to model size
e: Sustainability is part of responsible choices: right-size models and reuse pre-trained ones instead of training from scratch.

q: A model generates a fake quote attributed to a real public figure. Which risks does this create? (Choose TWO.)
e: Hallucinated claims about real people can mislead audiences, damage reputations and create legal exposure.

q: What does a 'denied topic' in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails do?
o: Makes the application refuse requests or responses about a defined subject
e: You describe the topic in natural language, with example phrases, and the guardrail blocks it.

q: Which practice supports accountability for AI decisions?
o: Logging model inputs, outputs and versions so decisions can be traced and audited
Deleting all logs after each request
Letting anyone change the model without records
e: Traceability (who, what model version, what data, what output) is essential for audits and fixing problems.

q: Which describes 'safety' as a responsible AI dimension?
o: Preventing harmful system output and misuse
Running the model on a safe server only
e: Safety covers harmful content, dangerous advice and misuse of the system.

q: Which is the best response when an AI system's errors could seriously affect people, such as in medical triage?
o: Keep a qualified human making or confirming the final decision
Fully automate decisions to remove human bias
Raise the temperature for more options
e: High-stakes uses need human oversight, validation and clear accountability.

q: Which describes the risk of 'over-reliance' on AI?
o: Users trusting AI output without checking it, even when it may be wrong
e: Design for appropriate trust: show sources and confidence, and encourage verification.

q: What should happen when a model's evaluation shows it performs much worse for one language group?
o: Investigate the data and model, improve coverage, and re-evaluate before wider release
Raise the temperature for that group
e: Performance gaps across groups are fairness issues to fix before deployment.
